thread.title: Iran's Strait of Hormuz Leverage Becomes Permanent Energy Weapon
thread.title_full: Iran's Strait of Hormuz Leverage Becomes Permanent Energy Weapon

author: CNN
title: Iran's Strait of Hormuz Leverage Becomes Permanent Energy Weapon
text:
Iran has secured a lasting strategic advantage by demonstrating its capability to blockade the Strait of Hormuz. Analysts warn this new reality introduces a permanent geopolitical risk premium into oil markets, reshapes global supply chains, and spurs alternative export routes, with long-term economic consequences far beyond any immediate conflict.
Iran has established a new and enduring form of leverage over the global economy through its demonstrated ability to effectively blockade the Strait of Hormuz, the world's most critical oil chokepoint.
Even if a diplomatic agreement is reached with the United States, analysts assert that this capability, which they liken to a "new nuclear option," cannot be stripped away. Before the current conflict, approximately one-fifth of the global supply of oil and liquefied natural gas passed through this waterway. The immediate threat of a complete closure has already contributed to a historic energy shock, but the long-term implications are even more profound.
The mere institutionalization of Iranian control, through bodies like the new Persian Gulf Strait Authority, introduces a permanent geopolitical risk premium into oil prices and undermines the previous assumption of unfettered access. The economic consequences extend far beyond the price of crude. While an open but Iran-managed strait would be less damaging than a total closure, the implementation of transit fees or bureaucratic vetting would ripple through global supply chains.
Goods ranging from fertilizer and jet fuel to helium and aluminum rely on stable energy markets and secure shipping lanes. Major oil traders and shipping companies are reportedly already making arrangements with Iran to secure passage, a desperate measure to replenish rapidly depleting global stockpiles. Energy consultancy Rystad estimates a persistent geopolitical risk premium of $10 to $20 per barrel, meaning the era of $60 oil is over for the foreseeable future, potentially lasting through 2027 and beyond.
In response to this permanent vulnerability, major Gulf producers are accelerating investments in alternative export routes to bypass the strait. Saudi Arabia uses the East-West pipeline, while the UAE employs the Habshan-Fujairah pipeline.
However, these alternatives have limited capacity and cannot fully replace the massive daily throughput of the Strait of Hormuz. The world faces a new reality where energy security is permanently compromised, and Iran holds a potent strategic card that will shape global economic and geopolitical dynamics for years to come, regardless of the outcome of any current ceasefire or deal
